observations: Wilson, Nassar & Gold (Neural Computation 2010) derived online Bayesian hazard-rate learning for change-point problems, supporting a direct posterior over environmental change rate instead of a hand-tuned surprise accumulator.

Piray & Daw (Nature Communications 2024) found humans can dissociate volatility from stochasticity from observations alone; their key statistical distinction is that volatility raises temporal autocorrelation whereas stochasticity reduces it despite both raising variance.

Pulcu & Browning (eLife 2025) found human learners adapt to volatility but can systematically misattribute outcome noise as volatility when their uncertainty representation is coarse. This is directly relevant to false change detections under overdispersed duration noise.

bounded_audit.scope: Synthetic bounded causal control continuing the prior SPLiT-derived latent-cause/dormant-memory branch. This is not an exact reproduction of SPLiT, Wilson-Nassar-Gold, Piray-Daw, or a neuroscience experiment.

design.semantic_cue: Noisy soft semantic-cause probability; cue-loss windows set semantic evidence to 0.5.
design.hand_accumulator_baseline: Alternative-vs-current duration log-likelihood ratio, decay=0.96, clipped per-event evidence, activation score>6 for 3 consecutive events; this mirrors the prior hand-designed duration-change gate family rather than reproducing its exact full four-hypothesis controller.
design.bayesian_fixed: Two-regime Bayesian filter with symmetric fixed hazard h=0.01, posterior decision threshold 0.97 for 2 consecutive events.
design.bayesian_adaptive: Same Bayesian filter, but hazard carries a discounted Beta posterior initialized at mean 0.01 with effective prior strength 200 and forgetting factor 0.995; each event updates hazard with posterior switch probability.
design.heldout: 96 paired seeds per change scenario, 800 events/seed. Stable stress probes use 200 held-out seeds. Paired bootstrap 95% intervals are over seed-level controller differences.

adaptive_vs_fixed_hazard.finding: Most of the gain came from maintaining a Bayesian regime posterior, not from online hazard learning itself.
adaptive_vs_fixed_hazard.interpretation: Adaptive hazard was neutral to modestly helpful in this bounded regime; do not attribute the large delay reduction specifically to hazard learning.

robust_contamination_probe.method: Add a regime-independent heavy-tail/outlier mixture component to each duration likelihood.
robust_contamination_probe.interpretation: Generic outlier robustness can suppress false volatility alarms but pays a substantial detection-latency cost. It is not retained as the preferred mechanism.

mechanistic_interpretation.positive: Replacing the hand-tuned duration surprise accumulator with a Bayesian regime posterior materially reduces activation delay across abrupt, cue-loss, prior-shift, overdispersed, gradual, and repeated-switch stress. Repeated-switch detection also becomes complete in this bounded test.
mechanistic_interpretation.negative_boundary: Online hazard learning adds only a small marginal benefit over a fixed-hazard Bayesian filter here. Stable overdispersion still occasionally produces false switches, and a simple heavy-tail contamination model reduces those false alarms only by slowing real change detection.
mechanistic_interpretation.neuroscience_connection: The remaining failure has the same computational form emphasized by recent human uncertainty-learning work: stochasticity/noise can be mistaken for volatility/change. Piray-Daw show that temporal structure/autocorrelation can distinguish these latent causes, while Pulcu-Browning show that coarse uncertainty representations cause noise-to-volatility misattribution. Therefore the next mechanism should infer duration stochasticity and regime volatility separately instead of converting all surprise into change evidence.
mechanistic_interpretation.memory_scope: This run did not re-run the actual fast PAST/GROUSE-like angular dormant-memory controller. The prior ultra-conservative fast restore remains provisional; slow Oja-like restore remains disabled.

limits: Synthetic geometric/mixture durations and a two-regime semantic model.
The Bayesian controller is a two-state online hazard filter, not full Adams-MacKay run-length BOCPD.
The adaptive hazard uses a discounted Beta approximation and fixed semantic emission model.
Overdispersion stress deliberately violates the detector likelihood family.
